subject: Follow-up: Crestview perf comparison & next lab tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@crestview.ai>, Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@crestview.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Crestview perf comparison & next lab tests

Hi Sophie / Marco —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: validate perceived latency delta vs Hyperscaler A/B under interactive load. Crestview cares most about p99 at high concurrency for the editor use case.
- Secondary: tokens/sec and cost-per-100k tokens comparison for our recommended config.
- Workloads: ~2.5–5s average responses today, mixed short/long contexts (200–2k tokens).

Proposed lab plan (high level)
1) Controlled A/B across three candidates: Redwood hosted (standard quant), Hyperscaler A (their managed endpoint), Hyperscaler B (managed), and a self-hosted open-model baseline.
2) Test matrix: concurrency sweep (1, 8, 16, 32), fixed prompt set (you shared sample), token budgets per request (avg 600 tokens), and long-context tail tests (2k tokens).
3) Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (aggregate and per-worker), error rate, and cost estimate normalized to token units.
4) Logistics: Redwood will coordinate test harness, produce the baseline runs, and share results + raw logs. We request a short window of API keys or a test tenant for Hyperscaler A/B if possible, or we can provide step-by-step to run on your side and ingest the outputs.

Ask for Crestview
- Please share the token sample you mentioned (prompt set + expected response length).
- Preferred maintenance window (we propose Tue/Wed mornings PST next week).
- Any constraints for data handling (PII, retention) we should be aware of.

Next steps (ownership)
- I will book a 2hr bench run on Tue morning to run the Redwood baseline and Hyperscaler A quick probe (Marissa to lead).
- Marissa / Logan to own the comparative runs; Rachel to add observability hooks.
- Sophie / Marco: please send the token sample and confirm an availability window.

Attachments: runbook stub and sample prompts referenced in call (attached as stubs).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_quick_bench_instructions.md (stub), crestview_prompt_list.txt (stub)

From: Sophie Martin <sophie@crestview.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@crestview.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:50:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Crestview perf comparison & next lab tests

Thanks Karthik — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority metric is p99 under sustained concurrency (32 simulated users). p95 matters but p99 is the gating factor for the editor experience.
- Cost: approximate token-normalized cost (per 100k tokens) is helpful but not a blocker for the first run.
- We are OK with Tue morning PST (May 31) for a 2hr window.

I've attached the prompt/sample file you asked for: crestview_token_sample.json (contains ~120 prompts with expected average output lengths). We can also provide short-lived keys for Hyperscaler A if that helps — I'll follow up with Marco.

One ask: can Redwood capture tail-latency histograms (p99.9 if easy) and include concurrency breakdowns in the report? Those are very helpful.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Platform | Crestview AI
Sophie Martin <sophie@crestview.ai>

Attachments: crestview_token_sample.json (1.2 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Crestview perf comparison & next lab tests

Looping in internal owners — thanks for the context, Karthik. Quick operational plan: 

- Marissa: I'll take Redwood baseline + Hyperscaler A probe (we have credits and a known config). Target: full sweep for concurrencies [1,8,16,32] by Tue morning.
- Logan: can you run Hyperscaler B + the open-model self-hosted baseline? Aim to produce a separate CSV with the same metric columns so we can merge.
- Rachel: please add the tracing hooks to the harness and ensure we capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9, tokens/sec, and per-request token counts. Also add a small dashboard (Grafana link) and a pointer to raw s3 logs.

Initial pass at thresholds for Crestview's use-case (subject to confirmation):
- p95 < 200 ms
- p99 < 450 ms
- tokens/sec > 800 (aggregate at concurrency 32)

Attachments: bench_runbook link (internal) — will drop to the shared Drive folder and add the checklist. Logan, please confirm you can run self-hosted variant by end of day Monday.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Hi Sophie / Marco —

All set for Tue 31 May, 08:00–10:00 PDT. Logistics and pre-reqs below: 

Pre-reqs for the session
- Crestview: if you can provide temporary test keys for Hyperscaler A (scoped/read-only) that will let us run the managed endpoint probe without asking your infra to run tests locally. If not, we'll provide a script you can run and return the CSV.
- We have your token sample (received) — thanks.
- Please confirm allowed IP ranges for outbound calls if you want us to hit an internal endpoint.

What we'll deliver after the window (by EOD Tue)
- A combined CSV with p50/p95/p99/p99.9, tokens/sec per run, and per-concurrency breakdown.
- A short readout doc (2–3 pages) with callouts on observed deltas, config differences, and a first-pass cost normalization.
- Raw logs and the Grafana link (internal access) mounted to the Drive folder.

Attachments: redwood_quick_bench_instructions.md (walkthrough), latency_p95p99_chart.png (example chart).

If anything changes on your side (window or keys), please ping me now so we can reschedule. Otherwise we'll proceed and share the readout Tuesday evening.

Cheers,
